title: Private deployments trust architecture and objection playbook
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact go-to-market messaging primer and objection-handling playbook for Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem) when selling to regulated buyers. It is meant for AE/SEs, solutions engineers, and product marketers preparing pitch decks, discovery responses, and RFP language.

Audience:
- Security-conscious buyers (infosec, cloud architecture, compliance)
- Procurement and legal teams at regulated enterprises
- Platform and infra teams evaluating control plane models and operational responsibilities

One‑line positioning (for intros):
Redwood Private gives teams the same high-performance inference runtime you use in hosted mode, delivered inside your network boundaries with explicit control plane semantics and enterprise-grade controls so you retain policy, telemetry, and audit ownership.

Elevator paragraph (2–3 sentences):
For regulated workloads, organizations need predictable inference economics and strict data controls without rebuilding the serving stack. Redwood Private ships the inference runtime and orchestration as a customer-managed environment (VPC or on-prem), plus an optional light control plane that surfaces telemetry and management hooks while keeping customer data and keys under the customer’s governance. This reduces compliance scope and preserves operator familiarity with cloud-native tooling.

Recommended control plane language (customer-friendly, contract-safe):
- "Customer-managed control plane": the control plane components are hosted in the customer’s VPC or in their on-prem infrastructure when requested. Redwood operates under our license/contract to provide upgrades and support, but the control plane endpoints are limited to your private network.
- "Management plane vs data plane": management/telemetry signals (metrics, model version metadata, health checks) flow through the control plane. Customer application payloads (prompts, embeddings, responses, keys) remain on-prem or in your VPC and are not routed to Redwood-hosted systems unless explicitly enabled.
- "Optional outbound telemetry": we recommend a short opt-in list for telemetry (non-sensitive metrics, anonymized error rates) to enable product support. Customers can choose the fields allowed and set retention and egress policies.
- "Bring your own KMS/Key custody": Redwood integrates with customer KMS/HSM. Keys never leave the customer-managed environment.

Security & compliance proof points (how to phrase):
- "Data residency and separation": all inference requests and model artifacts remain in the customer environment; we explicitly exclude customer payloads from Redwood-hosted storage when using Private.
- "Auditability": per-request audit logs available, with configurable retention and secure export (S3, internal SIEM).
- "Access control": integrates with SSO + RBAC; Admin/Operator roles are configurable, with support for fine-grained API tokens and short-lived certs.
- "Verifiable upgrades and images": signed runtime images and canary upgrade patterns; customers can vet images in a staging VPC prior to production rollout.

Top buyer objections and suggested short responses (copyable):
1) "We can't trust any external control plane — how do we know you're not seeing our prompts?"
   - Response: "With Redwood Private the control plane is deployed into your VPC or on-prem. By default, user payloads never leave your environment and we do not persist request contents in Redwood-hosted storage. You can also enable customer-managed KMS and configure telemetry to exclude payloads entirely."
2) "Who is responsible for incident response and SLAs?"
   - Response: "We operate on a shared-responsibility model. Redwood provides support for the runtime and will ship signed patches and runbooks; your infra team controls networking, host patching, and access. For dedicated contracts we include an SLA for runtime availability and a defined escalation path including 24/7 on-call."
3) "Is this going to be a maintenance burden for our infra team?"
   - Response: "Private is designed to be operationally light: we provide automation for upgrades, a reproducible deployment artifact, and docs for common ops tasks. For customers who want a fully self-managed flow we provide an on-prem bundle; for others we offer a managed operator model where Redwood runs the control plane inside your project under a narrow support access window."
4) "How do you compare to X that is fully self-hosted/open-source?"
   - Response: "If you need white-box control and to build everything yourself, open-source runtimes work. The difference is we ship a production-focused serving runtime, integration with model operational patterns (prefix caching, kv cache management, and cost-aware batching), and an opinionated set of controls that shortens time to production while preserving governance."

Competitive differentiation (messaging hooks):
- Operational parity: "Same API and behavior across hosted, dedicated, and private — reduces rework and regression risk."
- Production-focused runtime: "Optimized kernels, runtime batching, and model-aware routing that open-source projects seldom ship ready-for-scale."
- Flexible control plane: "Tunably light — customers decide telemetry and management exposure instead of a binary hosted vs self-hosted choice."
- Cost visibility + unit economics: "Token-level cost breakdown and per-model cost attribution available in Private with the same toolset as hosted users."

Mini battle cards (one-line counters):
- Competitor: Generic cloud managed endpoints -> Counter: "We offer a patterns-first runtime that optimizes per-token cost and latency for LLMs, not just GPU provisioning."
- Competitor: Self-hosted OSS runtime -> Counter: "Less lift to go from POC to SLA-backed production; we include rollout tooling, signed images, and observability tailored to inference."
- Competitor: On-prem consulting houses -> Counter: "Standardized artifacts and upgrade paths reduce knowledge silos and long-term lock-in to consultants."

Language for legal/contract/IA teams (short bullets):
- Data processing: "We will not process or store customer request payloads outside of customer-managed infrastructure unless explicitly enabled in writing."
- Access: "Support access is role-limited and auditable; emergency access requires two-party authorization and is logged."
- Liability and indemnities: "Use standard enterprise language; refer to SOW for managed operator scope or to the licensing schedule for self-managed bundles."

Sales enablement snippets (for slides / emails):
- Slide headline: "Run inference where your data needs to stay — with cloud-grade performance."
- Email subject line: "Private inference with explicit control plane options for regulated workloads"
- Open line: "We provide a consistent inference runtime behind your firewall or within your VPC so your compliance and platform teams keep the keys — while your engineers keep the same API."

Discovery checklist (questions for prospect calls):
- Which compliance regimes are relevant (HIPAA, FedRAMP, PCI, GDPR data residency)?
- Do you require customer KMS/HSM integration?
- Is a fully offline air-gapped deployment required, or can you provide controlled egress for telemetry?
- Who owns OS/host patching and node lifecycle?
- Expected QPS/latency SLOs and model sizes (for capacity planning)

Example short objection-response script (for SE roleplay):
- Buyer: "We need FedRAMP High — can you comply?"
- SE: "We have customers using Private to meet FedRAMP requirements by combining our private control plane with customer-managed KMS and an audited deployment pipeline. We can map our controls to your FedRAMP checklist and identify any residual controls that your team would need to cover."

Next steps / tactical asks for GTM teams:
- Create a short one-pager tailored to regulated verticals (healthcare, financial services, gov) using the above proof points.
- Produce a support-runbook template and upload as a linked artifact for SEs to attach to proposals.
- Build a short demo flow that shows: (1) KMS binding, (2) toggling telemetry fields, (3) an upgrade canary in a staging VPC.

Appendix: sample telemetry field whitelist (recommended defaults)
- node.cpu_util, node.gpu_util, inference.latency.p50/p95, model_version, error.count, request.size.aggregate (no payloads), anonymized_error_codes

This doc is intentionally compact — aim to copy/paste lines into decks, response templates, and RFPs. For longer technical appendices (network diagrams, install steps, detailed SOC2/ISO mappings) link to the private-deployments ops repo and Confluence artifacts referenced above.

Author notes:
- Drafted after SE feedback loop and two recent regulated buyer discovery calls (Q4 2024).
- Objective: reduce back-and-forth on control plane semantics and make SEs confident answering the 5 common operational objections.
